case.summary: Case HHG-011 on card C11923-K2 (customer C11923) is assessed as uncertain at a fraud probability of 0.60, with the episode limited to the single disputed transaction 3583368, an online $131.30 product-C purchase on 2016-12-29, so exposure is $131.30. The candidate pattern is card_not_present_new_device: the flagged device profile is brand-new to this card (first-ever use), matching the label convention used in six of this card's prior confirmed-fraud cases (CC-3905, CC-3206, CC-3039, CC-4501). The decisive evidence is a genuine conflict between two families: the customer's denial plus this card's chronic fraud memory (10 of 11 prior closed cases confirmed fraud) argue fraud, while the very low calibrated cms_p (0.0428) and the earlier cleared "new phone" case CC-4743 on this same card argue legitimacy; no shared-device or ring evidence (R6) or matching card-testing chain (R5) was found to break the tie. We asked for step-up authentication on the online transaction and assumed (simulated) it went unanswered within the window, so per R4 the recommendation is now MONITOR_CARD plus DECLINE_TRANSACTION on the pending authorization (route L1), with the case kept open (CREATE_CASE) and escalated to an analyst (ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST) under R8 for the unresolved conflict; no SAR is filed at this exposure and pattern strength. The alternative reading is that this is simply routine, if erratic, account behavior — the card processes thousands of small online purchases and even shows recurring same-amount charges to gmail.com and hotmail.com, though neither group satisfies the R7 monthly-cadence gate, so the recurring-charge exception does not apply and the dispute is treated as a live alert pending the analyst's review and any customer follow-up.
